summary: Repeated 429 waves after scale-up: HTTP/2 multiplex and token-refill skew on Dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary:
BrightCart began seeing recurring 429 waves across multiple services immediately after a Dedicated pool scale-up event at ~2026-03-10T02:10:00Z. The waves manifest as clustered 429 responses for ~3-8 minutes following host additions and then subside, only to reappear on subsequent scale events. Impact: production customers experienced degraded throughput and failed upload jobs (embeds + short chat requests) for the duration of the waves.

Impact:
- Several background bulk-embed jobs failed and retried concurrently (customer reported increase in error rate from 0.2% -> 4.6%).
- Interactive chat latency spiked and some calls returned 429s, affecting UI experience for a subset of users (approx 3-5% of active sessions).

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (customer-owned reservation) in prod-us-east (us-east-1)
- API access over multiplexed HTTP/2 (gRPC-web) via customer edge proxy
- Autoscaler added 6 hosts during the observed window (scale-up from 12 -> 18 GPUs)

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Start sustained mixed workload: N = 400 concurrent clients (mix of short chat + batch embed streams).
2) Trigger autoscaler policy by gradually increasing throughput for ~10 minutes.
3) Observe scale-up event and host join logs in autoscaler.
4) Immediately after host join, see clustered 429s on a subset of client connections for 3-8 minutes; then normal traffic resumes.

Observed behavior:
- 429 responses include X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 and Retry-After headers of varying values (30-90s).
- Throttle metrics show per-connection token buckets being depleted quickly; refill counters on newly joined hosts are offset relative to origin.
- HTTP/2 connection reuse patterns concentrate many logical streams onto a few long-lived connections; when a new host joins, edge-to-origin affinity changes and tokens are not rebalanced smoothly.

Expected behavior:
- After scale-up the system should rebalance load without producing transient tenant-wide 429 waves; tokens/refill epochs should remain aligned and credits should not be double-counted or lost during host join.

Logs / quick traces (redacted):
- api-gateway: 2026-03-10T02:12:18Z WARN ingress: "token-window-mismatch detected for api_key=acct-brightcart-44" host_join_id=host-17
- rate-limiter: 2026-03-10T02:12:19Z INFO refill: "epoch_offset=+42s" host=host-17 tenant=acct-brightcart-44
- ingress-proxy: 2026-03-10T02:13:02Z ERROR connection: "http2 stream reset after 429 flood" session_id=svc-8fc

Additional context:
- Customer uses a pool of long-lived HTTP/2 connections through a caching edge proxy; connections are sticky to a small set of origin hosts for affinity.
- Customer reported they recently changed client-side connection pooling to hold connections open for longer (to reduce handshake overhead).

Customer request:
- BrightCart asks for guidance and a fix path to prevent these recurring 429 waves during future scale events and for an explanation of root cause.

investigation_notes: Triage: Issue reproducible in internal lab when using long-lived HTTP/2 streams and spinning up additional origin processes while request fanout is high.

Hypothesis: Refill epoch used by token accounting was anchored to host-local clock at process start. When hosts join at different offsets, per-host refill epochs will be misaligned. HTTP/2 multiplexing concentrates logical streams on fewer connections exposing tenant-wide credit spikes when affinity shifts.

Metrics: Grafana panels show step increases in 'throttle_count' immediately after host join events and a correlated nonzero 'epoch_offset_seconds' metric on new hosts (values 20-65s). Dashboard links: https://grafana.redwood/boards/rate-limiter/refill-epoch .
Edge behavior: Customer edge proxy rebalances streams to different origins on host join, causing an instantaneous re-allocation of active streams to hosts with depleted or offset buckets.
Risk assessment: High for dedicated customers who use long-lived HTTP/2 connections and aggressive autoscaling. Low risk for short-lived HTTP/1 clients.
Mitigation tested: Client-side jitter + staggered reconnect reduces severity but does not fully eliminate short windows of 429s during rapid scale-ups.

Engineering plan: 1) Normalize refill epoch to tenant-level master clock (short-term fix). 2) Add 'host-join grace window' that borrows a small portion of credits from existing hosts until local refill aligns (safety limits applied). 3) Postmortem and guidance doc for design considerations with long-lived HTTP/2 connections.
Timeline: Patch PR opened 2026-03-13; target canary deploy same day; full rollout pending verification across canary hosts for 24h.
resolution:
Workaround (applied): customer reduced connection stickiness and added per-client jitter on reconnects; error frequency decreased.
Permanent fix (in progress): merged a patch to align token-refill epochs to tenant-level clock and added a short host-join grace credit transfer. Canary started 2026-03-13; initial telemetry promising.
Post-deploy actions: complete full rollout, publish runbook for dedicated customers with long-lived connections, and schedule a joint postmortem with BrightCart to review mitigations and recommended client settings.
follow_up_actions: Complete global rollout of refill-epoch alignment patch (ENG-#RL-1492)
Publish guidance: 'Dedicated pools + long-lived HTTP/2: connection pooling and autoscale best practices' in support docs
Create an automated canary monitor alert for 'epoch_offset_seconds' spikes on host join events
Schedule postmortem meeting with BrightCart and engineering (invite: brightcart-cs@brightcart.com)
